advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm whether unbounded free-form prose under `## Acceptance Criteria` is an intended exemption; if not, charge non-checklist AC lines or bound the AC block.
evidence: det_floor.py:345-346: `if not in_ac:` / `charged += len(line)` — lines while in_ac are never charged

det_floor.py:332-334 docstring claims AC is 'independently bounded by AC count plus P8's whole-context budget', but P4_AC_SOFT_CAP counts checklist items and per det_floor.py:23 'AC count ... remain advisory' (never blocks)
_count_ac_items counts only `- [ ]`/`- [x]` items (det_floor.py:190-194), so non-checklist prose under the heading is neither counted nor charged
advisory.finding: review_bounded_description_chars exempts ALL content inside the `## Acceptance Criteria` block (everything from the AC heading to the next `## ` heading or EOF) from the P4 cap, not just checklist items. Because the AC-count signal (P4_AC_SOFT_CAP) counts checklist items and is only advisory (never blocks), arbitrary free-form prose placed under the AC heading is entirely uncharged and unblocked — a bypass of the plan-review admission cap.
scenarios: An author moves narration under `## Acceptance Criteria` (or appends it after the AC block when AC is the last section) to regain admission without shortening actual prose

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reuse the canonical fenced-aware AC/H2 parser (evaluate_plan_clarity) for charge-boundary detection rather than a separate regex scan.
evidence: det_floor.py:340,343: bespoke `re.fullmatch(r"##[ \t]+Acceptance Criteria...")` and `re.fullmatch(r"##[ \t]+.+?...")` scan every line with no fence tracking
_plan_clarity.py:130-148: canonical parser tracks `fence` state (`_fence_marker`) and only calls `_heading` on non-fenced lines
_plan_clarity.py:16: `_H2_RE = ^##[ \t]+(.+?)[ \t]*$` is the shared H2 definition the AC parser uses
advisory.finding: review_bounded_description_chars re-implements heading/AC-block detection with its own line-by-line regex instead of reusing the canonical evaluate_plan_clarity/_H2_RE parser, and does not account for fenced code blocks. A `## `-looking line inside a fenced code block in the description is treated as a heading (AC-start or AC-end), diverging from the parser the rest of the DET floor uses and mis-charging characters.
scenarios: A description with a fenced code sample containing a line like `## Acceptance Criteria` or `## Example` flips in_ac state incorrectly, over- or under-charging the cap
advisory.suggested_fix: Derive the charged span from the same section/fence-tracking parser used by _count_ac_items so heading and code-fence semantics stay in lockstep.
